subject: Audit scope question: control coverage when requests traverse fallback routing or private connectors
messages:
From: Martin Liu <security@equitybank.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@equitybank.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC2 coverage & evidence request for routing/connector flows

Hi Logan,

We're in the final stages of Equity Bank's vendor SOC 2 review and a couple of items came up specific to routing between deployment modes. Can you confirm whether Redwood's SOC 2 Type II for the 2026 period covers the following flows, and if not, what evidence you can provide?

1) Requests that are pinned to a Dedicated pool but are automatically failed over to Hosted (shared) during capacity bursts — do those Hosted-handled requests fall under the same SOC2 period/controls or need a bridge letter?

2) Private/VPN connector flows where traffic enters a VPC-connected deployment (customer-managed network) but then calls back to a Redwood routing service for model selection — does that callback path get audited as part of Type II?

3) SIG/CAIQ: we also have a short SIG questionnaire for routing, tenant isolation, and sampling of routing logs. Can you provide a completed CAIQ or SIG partial answers for these areas?

For audit purposes we need: the SOC2 report (redacted if needed), any bridge letter that explains scope gaps for 2026, a short routing diagram, and a sample of routing audit logs (redacted request ids ok). Our timeline is tight — can you confirm what you can provide by the end of next week?

Thanks,
Martin Liu
Director, Information Security
Equity Bank

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Martin Liu <security@equitybank.com>, procurement@equitybank.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC2 coverage & evidence request for routing/connector flows

Martin — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Kimberly (Security) and Neha (Compliance) to confirm precise artifacts and timing.

High-level answer up front: Dedicated pools that are strictly pinned and never route to shared Hosted are covered fully by the Type II. When automatic fallback to Hosted occurs, the control boundary can be split depending on whether customer data transits shared environments; that typically requires a bridge letter to explain the partial coverage/windowed exception. Private connectors (VPC/on-prem) are usually in-scope for controls that run in the private control plane, but callbacks that traverse public routing layers need evidence.

Kimberly/Neha — can you confirm what we can produce: SOC2-2026 (redacted PDF), a bridge letter for the audit window 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31 if needed, a routing diagram and tenant mapping, and a 1-2 hour slice of routing audit logs with request ids redacted? Also, the customer asked for SIG/CAIQ fragments covering routing and multitenancy — do we have a prefilled SIG file we can share or do we need to build a bespoke response?

Logan
VP, Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Martin Liu <security@equitybank.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC2 coverage & evidence request for routing/connector flows

Hi Martin — thanks, Logan. Quick summary and what we can provide this week: 

- Dedicated vs Hosted fallback: If a workload is explicitly pinned to a Dedicated pool (customer-reserved GPUs, tenant-isolated runtime), controls covering access, change management, logging, and tenant isolation in that pool are included in the Type II report for the audit period. If the customer's traffic is configured to allow automatic failover to Hosted shared capacity, the Hosted-handled tokens are treated as a separate environment for audit boundary purposes. For 2026 we issued a bridge letter for a small set of customers where ephemeral fallback occurred — that artifact explains which control areas remain covered and which require compensating controls.

- Private/VPC connectors: The customer-managed network endpoints and private control plane are in-scope when the Redwood control plane components that enforce controls (auth, routing decisions, logging collectors) operate inside that boundary. If the callback crosses into Redwood-hosted routing (public control plane), we classify the call path as partially in-scope and provide evidence (routing diagrams + sampled logs).

What we can attach now (already in draft / available):
- routing-diagram.svg (high-level topology showing Dedicated pools, Hosted fallback path, and VPC connectors) (attachment: routing-diagram.svg)
- tenant-mapping.csv (pseudonymized mapping used for audit sampling) (attachment: tenant-mapping.csv)

Requested evidence we will produce by 2027-05-21: 
1) Redacted SOC2 Type II report for 2026 (PDF) — redaction limited to internal service-owner emails and auditor notes.
2) Bridge letter covering the documented fallbacks during the audit window (if Equity Bank had fallback allowed for their workload we will explicitly call that out).
3) 1–2 hour redacted routing log sample including routing decision metadata (request ids hashed) and timestamps.

A couple of questions for your team to speed this:
- Do you require raw request payloads (we recommend against sharing payloads; we can provide metadata/traces only).
- For the SIG/CAIQ: do you want our completed CAIQ (we have a standard CAIQ with redactions) or a smaller SIG routing addendum?

On the latter, if you can confirm which you prefer we will include it in the package to deliver by Friday.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Security Assurance
Redwood Inference

From: Martin Liu <security@equitybank.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@equitybank.com
Date: Wed, 18 May 2027 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC2 coverage & evidence request for routing/connector flows

Kimberly — thanks, this is helpful. A couple of clarifications from our auditor: 

- For fallback: Equity Bank does not permit request payloads containing PCI or full PAN data to traverse shared Hosted pools. We only allow model inference calls with tokenized/PII-stripped inputs to have fallback. Can you confirm whether your sampling will indicate whether a request was payload-restricted at routing time (i.e., a routing flag)?

- Private connector callback: if we implement a VPN connector for vector-indexing (i.e., we keep vectors in our VPC) but call Redwood for model selection that matches vectors to a hosted model, will the callback metadata (which model was selected and the model variant) appear in your routing logs so auditors can verify the decision path without seeing payload?

Finally, can you provide the SOC2 PDF + bridge letter as soon as possible — even a redacted PDF and a signed bridge letter (scannable PDF) will allow us to progress with Legal while your log slice and CAIQ arrive.

Thanks,
Martin

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Martin Liu <security@equitybank.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 May 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC2 coverage & evidence request for routing/connector flows

Martin — attaching the initial package for checkout.

Attachments included (redacted where necessary):
- SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-2026-redacted.pdf (attachment: SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-2026-redacted.pdf)
- bridge-letter-20260101-20261231.pdf (attachment: bridge-letter-20260101-20261231.pdf)
- routing-diagram.svg (attachment already shared)
- tenant-mapping.csv (attachment already shared)

Notes: 
- The routing log slice will be prepared and delivered under a restricted SFTP link (we will hash request ids and strip payload fields). Expected delivery: 2027-05-21.
- For fallback requests we emit a routing_flag that indicates "pinned" vs "fallback_to_hosted" and a payload_classification tag (e.g., tokenized, pii-stripped, sensitive). Auditors can use these fields to verify whether fallback requests had restricted payloads without seeing raw content.
- For private connector callbacks we record model_selection metadata (model_id and variant) and routing decision entries; these are included in the routing trace metadata without payloads.

Related hubspot ticket: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/EB-4729
Internal runbook (for auditors): https://docs.redwood.com/runbooks/audit-routing-handling

If Equity Bank is comfortable with the redacted SOC2 and the signed bridge letter we attached, please confirm and we'll finalize the log slice and the SIG/CAIQ fragment (we have a standard CAIQ export ready to redact).

Thanks and happy to hop on a quick call if your auditor wants a walkthrough.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Compliance & Controls
Redwood Inference
